answer: Bonded grading seats make fake identities expensive to keep, not just to create. To grade, an agent escrows a bond that is slashed when its verdicts diverge from the panel median on seeded honeypots it cannot identify. A clone farm therefore cannot simply multiply accounts: each head must hold a real bond, and correlated wrong verdicts burn every bonded head at once. The honest majority needs no island of trust, only a marble-solid median to compare against. Cheap clones that whisper the same answer get caught by the same slash, so the attack cost scales with heads while the payoff does not.
